server.name: A label for this server in the app. It is not sent in any request.
server.port: The local port the server listens on (127.0.0.1 only). The issuer and endpoint URLs are built from it.
server.issuerUrl: The server's base URL. Clients use it as the issuer, and its metadata is served at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
server.authorizationUrl: Where clients send the browser for the authorization code flow (GET /authorize).
server.tokenUrl: Where clients exchange credentials, codes, or refresh tokens for tokens (POST /token).
server.clients: Client ID and secret pairs registered with this server. Import copies one into a new client configuration.
server.clientId: Generated ID a client sends to identify itself to this server.
server.clientSecret: Generated secret a client sends with its client ID to authenticate at the token endpoint.
server.users: Accounts that can sign in on the login page when user-based access is on.
server.resource: A protected endpoint for testing tokens. Call it with an access token in an Authorization: Bearer header.

serverSettings.redirectUrlOverride: When set, the server redirects here after authorization instead of to the redirect_uri the client sent. Must be an absolute http(s) URL.
serverSettings.accessTokenExpiry: Lifetime of issued access tokens, in seconds. Sets the JWT exp claim and expires_in in the token response.
serverSettings.refreshTokenExpiry: Lifetime of issued refresh tokens, in seconds. Refresh tokens are only issued when the scope includes offline_access.
serverSettings.userBased: When on, /authorize shows a login page instead of a consent page, and issued tokens carry the signed-in username.

serverUser.username: The name the user signs in with on the login page. Leading and trailing spaces are removed.
serverUser.password: The password the user signs in with. It is stored and shown as plain text, since this is a test tool.
serverUser.userData: Text that GET /resource returns as userData for tokens issued to this user. Leave empty for the default.

clientConfig.name: A label for this configuration in the app. It is not sent in any request.
clientConfig.issuerUrl: Base URL of the authorization server. Server metadata is fetched from <issuer>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
clientConfig.useServerMetadata: Fill the authorization and token URLs from the server's RFC 8414 metadata instead of typing them in.
clientConfig.authorizationUrl: The server's authorization endpoint. The browser is opened here for the authorization code flow.
clientConfig.tokenUrl: The server's token endpoint, where codes, client credentials, and refresh tokens are exchanged for tokens.
clientConfig.clientId: The client ID registered with the authorization server. Sent as client_id.
clientConfig.clientSecret: The client secret registered with the authorization server. Sent as client_secret in the request body.
clientConfig.scopes: Space-separated scopes to request. Include offline_access to get a refresh token from servers that support it.
clientConfig.scopesSupported: Scopes the server lists in its metadata (scopes_supported).
clientConfig.grantType: Authorization Code opens a browser so a user can approve access, then exchanges the code (with PKCE) for tokens. Client Credentials requests a token directly with the client ID and secret, with no user involved.
clientConfig.callbackUrl: The redirect_uri this app listens on for the authorization code. The server must allow it, or redirect here through an override.
clientConfig.extraParams: Extra parameters added to the authorization, token, and client credentials requests, such as audience or resource.
clientConfig.metadata: The server's RFC 8414 authorization server metadata, fetched from the issuer's well-known URL.

paramSection.authorize: Parameters sent to the authorization endpoint. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.
paramSection.token: Parameters sent when exchanging the authorization code. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.
paramSection.send: Parameters sent in the client credentials token request. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.
paramSection.refresh: Parameters sent when using the stored refresh token. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.

param.response_type: Always code: asks the server for an authorization code.
param.grant_type: Tells the token endpoint which kind of grant is being exchanged.
param.client_id: Identifies the client to the server.
param.client_secret: Authenticates the client to the server, sent in the request body.
param.redirect_uri: Where the server sends the browser back with the code. The token request must repeat the same value.
param.state: A random value the server echoes back, checked on return to protect against forged callbacks.
param.code_challenge: PKCE: a SHA-256 hash of the code verifier, sent with the authorization request.
param.code_challenge_method: PKCE: how the code challenge was derived. Always S256.
param.code_verifier: PKCE: the secret behind the code challenge, proving the token request comes from the same client.
param.refresh_token: The stored refresh token being exchanged for a new access token.
